lead_verbatim: Five companies presented in the lipid session, and between them they described three answers to the problem Professor Annelise Dahlberg had named in her opening remarks: a twice-yearly injection against lipoprotein(a), a once-daily oral inhibitor of PCSK9, and a once-yearly injection against the same target. The figures were large and the comparators were placebo. The clinicians on the panel accepted the biology and questioned the follow-up.

paragraphs.text_verbatim: Rachel Adeyemi of Vantrel Bio set out the case for lipoprotein(a) as a target: a survey of cardiologists found that 63% never test for it, and the company's phase 2 study reported a reduction of 94% at week 48. Jonas Keller of Marlowe Pharma reported a 61% reduction in LDL cholesterol at week 12 with the oral inhibitor pendrelvarin, and Miriam Castellanos of Arden Therapeutics reported that a single dose of ancelsiran held LDL cholesterol 52% lower at 12 months. Tobias Hartmann of Solenne Biologics presented an antibody against ANGPTL3, and Priya Raman of Ravensworth Medical a coronary sinus reducer for refractory angina. No outcomes data were presented by any company; the one outcomes trial described, SILVERBIRCH-1, reads out in the second half of 2027.
paragraphs.notes: Footnote 1 is anchored after '...reduction of 94% at week 48.'; footnote 2 after '...52% lower at 12 months.'

sections.heading: Lipoprotein(a) is the new target, and the outcomes are two years away

paragraphs.text_verbatim: Vantrel's position, raised in several sessions, is that a large population is untreated because it is untested. Adeyemi reported that 88% of patients in the phase 2 BIRCHWOOD study of 240 patients reached a lipoprotein(a) level below 125 nmol/L, and that the phase 3 SILVERBIRCH-1 trial of 8,240 patients, with a primary endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events, is fully enrolled with a readout "late next year". A substudy in 120 patients reported a 9% fall in plaque volume.
paragraphs.notes: Footnote 3 is anchored after '"late next year".'; footnote 4 after '...9% fall in plaque volume.'

paragraphs.text_verbatim: On the panel Professor Oskar Weiland asked whether plaque regression translates into fewer events. Adeyemi said that it is a hypothesis. That exchange is the state of the evidence: a biomarker lowered by more than 90%, a structural change of single figures, and no outcome yet. Kenji Okada of Harbourline Capital, speaking on the investor panel, named lipids as a crowded indication in which understanding one's place in the landscape is the critical question.

sections.heading: Oral and annual dosing compete on the same target

paragraphs.text_verbatim: Two companies presented PCSK9 inhibition in forms that do not resemble each other. Marlowe's pendrelvarin is a once-daily tablet. The phase 2b LANTANA study of 410 patients reported the 61% reduction above, and three phase 3 studies, GRANITE-1, GRANITE-2 and GRANITE-3, began in the third quarter of 2026 on top of statin therapy, with readouts in 2028. Keller described them as "about 2,400 patients each".

Arden's ancelsiran is a once-yearly injection. The phase 2 WINTERGREEN study of 112 patients reported the 52% reduction at 12 months after a single dose, and the phase 3 FALCONER study of 3,000 patients is to start in the first quarter of 2027, shown on the slide. Castellanos stated that patients from the phase 1 study have 7 years of follow-up.

Two company videos were played. In the first, four named clinicians stated that 95% of patients achieve annual dosing and 93% prefer it to monthly injections, without naming a trial; the second carried patient quotations with the on-screen notice that the voices were actor portrayals. On the panel Castellanos said that patients with 6 years of follow-up are on their sixth annual dose and that the company has "seen up to 20 doses" in the open-label cohort, which the follow-up period does not allow.
paragraphs.notes: Footnote 7 is anchored after '...actor portrayals.'; footnote 8 after '...does not allow.' The word 'open-label' is hyphenated across a line break in the source ('open-' / 'label'); the plain-text extraction runs it together as 'openlabel'.

paragraphs.text_verbatim: The point raised most often by clinicians, in this session and in the arrhythmia session, was that a longer interval between doses is not an interval between visits. Professor Sofia Esteves stated that no data support leaving a patient unseen for six months, and that in her reading of the earlier data about half of patients in phase 2 needed uptitration. Professor Elena Marchetti put the proportion of patients who do not reach their LDL goal on a statin alone at "at least 30 to 40%", without a source. Nobody proposed abandoning statins, and the consensus of the panel was that combinations and longer dosing intervals are additions to the foundation rather than replacements for it.

Vantrel's own real-world claim cut both ways. Adeyemi reported that 47% of patients on injectable lipid therapy are non-persistent by year five, citing a 2025 analysis. The figure supports the case for a less frequent injection, and it also describes the population a less frequent injection will be given to.
paragraphs.notes: Footnote 10 is anchored after '...citing a 2025 analysis.'

sections.heading: Beyond LDL: an antibody and a device

paragraphs.text_verbatim: Solenne's tirocimab, an antibody against ANGPTL3 given monthly, reported a 49% reduction in LDL cholesterol at week 24 in 48 patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, and a 54% reduction in triglycerides in a phase 2a study in mixed dyslipidaemia. Hartmann stated that injection site reactions occurred in "under 3%" of patients and that a depot formulation of an oral follow-on compound, SOL-440, could release drug for up to six months; both statements were spoken only and the compound is preclinical.
paragraphs.notes: Paragraph runs from page 13 to page 14; footnote 11 is anchored after '...mixed dyslipidaemia.' on page 14.

paragraphs.text_verbatim: Ravensworth's CSR-2 coronary sinus reducer is CE-marked. In the sham-controlled HARBOURLIGHT study, 71% of patients improved by at least one angina class at six months against 45% with sham. Raman stated that the US pivotal study is fully enrolled with a readout in the second quarter of 2027. She also said that the first-generation device "may be more suitable for patients with microvascular angina", where her own description a minute earlier made clear that the second-generation device was meant.
paragraphs.notes: Footnote 12 is anchored after '...against 45% with sham.'; footnote 13 after '...was meant.'

key_point_verbatim: Key point. The headline reductions in this chapter cannot be ranked against one another. Each was measured at a different time point against placebo in a different population, and only one programme has an outcomes trial under way.
matters_not_addressed_verbatim: No price was given for any product. No speaker proposed a monitoring schedule for twice-yearly or annual dosing. The comparator in every efficacy figure was placebo on top of statin, and no company compared itself with another. The panel did not discuss how a once-yearly injection would be recorded and followed in routine records, and no payer or health economist was on the programme.
matters_not_addressed_notes: The word 'twice-yearly' is hyphenated across a line break in the source ('twice-' / 'yearly'); the plain-text extraction runs it together as 'twiceyearly'.
